edges.description: The cell responds by downregulating GLS and upregulating glutamine synthetase, but the compensation is insufficient.
Hyperactive glutaminase over-converts glutamine to glutamate.
Compensation is insufficient to prevent the amino acid imbalance.
Hypermorphic GLS expression reduces the capacity to detoxify reactive oxygen species.
The glutamine-to-glutamate shift propagates through the TCA cycle, transamination, and nucleotide metabolism.
White matter is affected, consistent with the elevated glutamate measured in white matter as well as grey matter.
Reduced reactive-oxygen-species detoxification provides the proposed redox route from Ser482Cys-GLS expression to cataract formation.
Lens opacification manifests clinically as early-onset bilateral cataract.

nodes.description: Because glutaminase sits at the junction of many pathways, its hyperactivity remodels the metabolome well beyond the glutamine/glutamate pair. In a HEK293 model tuning GLS activity, 109 endogenously relevant metabolite features were significantly affected: TCA-cycle intermediates rose with a truncation of the cycle at citrate; transamination products, proline and ornithine synthesis, and GABA metabolism increased; and asparagine and nucleotide metabolites — notably pyrimidine/thymine metabolites — fell in step with glutamine. This positions the disorder as a broad metabolic perturbation rather than a single-metabolite excess, and plausibly underlies the mild hyperammonemia and the raised brain alanine and lactate reported in the patient.

nodes.description: The primary lesion is a heterozygous de novo missense variant, p.Ser482Cys, in GLS. Ser482 is not itself a catalytic residue but is conserved to the same degree as the catalytic residues across roughly 12,000 GLS sequences from more than 1,000 genera — evidence that its identity is under strong selection precisely because it tunes enzyme activity downward.

The review's clinical table further records it as bilateral and neonatal in onset, while the original report titles it an infantile cataract; that laterality and timing detail comes from a table cell rather than a quotable sentence, so it is described here rather than carried as an evidence snippet.

nodes.description: Cells mount a two-armed homeostatic response to the hyperactive enzyme: compensatory downregulation of GLS expression, and upregulation of the counteracting enzyme glutamine synthetase, which runs the reverse reaction (glutamate to glutamine). The persistence of severe glutamate excess and glutamine depletion in patient tissues shows this compensation to be insufficient. The presence of the compensatory response is itself part of the evidence for pathogenicity, since it demonstrates the cell registers the variant as a perturbation.

nodes.description: De novo heterozygous missense variant substituting cysteine for the highly conserved serine at position 482 of glutaminase. Not a catalytic residue, but conserved to the same degree as the catalytic residues; the substitution is proposed to improve the electrostatic environment of the catalytic site and thereby raise activity.

nodes.description: Hyperactive glutaminase drives excessive conversion of glutamine to glutamate. Increased glutamate with decreased glutamine was measured in urine and in fibroblasts, and the imbalance is far more extreme in brain, where magnetic resonance spectroscopic imaging showed extremely high glutamate in both grey and white matter with glutamine almost undetectable. This is the exact biochemical inverse of the hyperglutaminemia of glutaminase deficiency. Notably the imbalance is compartment-dependent: cerebrospinal-fluid glutamate and glutamine were reported as unremarkable even while brain-tissue spectroscopy was grossly abnormal, so a normal CSF amino acid profile does not exclude the diagnosis.

nodes.description: Glutamate is neurotoxic in excess (excitotoxicity), and the brain glutamate concentrations measured in this patient were strikingly high. The original authors advance this as the explanation for the profound developmental delay. Note the direction of the claim: this is the same neurotransmitter whose deficiency is invoked in GLS loss-of-function disease, so glutaminase disorders damage the brain from either direction.

nodes.description: Pharmacological GLS inhibition is the mechanistically rational therapy for a hypermorphic GLS allele, and glutaminase inhibitors already exist in oncology. Proof of concept is limited to the zebrafish model, where GLS inhibition alleviated the cataract phenotype. This has NOT been tested in humans with this disorder, and no dosing, safety, or efficacy data in patients exist — it is recorded here as a mechanistic lead, not a treatment recommendation.

nodes.description: Expression of the hypermorphic Ser482Cys allele reduces the capacity to detoxify reactive oxygen species. Because cataract is a known consequence of oxidative stress, this provides the mechanistic route from a glutamine metabolism defect to a lens phenotype — a connection that is otherwise non-obvious.

nodes.description: Ser482Cys is proposed to improve the electrostatic environment of the glutaminase catalytic site, intrinsically inducing hyperactivity. This is a qualitative change in regulation rather than a simple quantitative increase: the enzyme is driven above the submaximal activity that evolutionary constraint on Ser482 appears designed to maintain, and the cell's homeostatic responses (see the compensatory node) fail to restore balance.
